pr_title: kubeadm should ignore cgroup driver check on Windows node
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug
/sig windows
/sig cluster-lifecycle
/area kubeadm

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

> kubeadm doesn't do anything about cgroup drivers on Windows because cgroups don't exist on Windows.
>  ideally the kubelet checks about this should be skipped entirely in dockershim for non-Linux.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #97759

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

issue_context.title: kubelet: don't check for the Docker cgroup driver on Windows
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

I have a Kubernetes Cluster with 2 Windows Server 2019 Core VMs as worker nodes. I upgraded first the cluster, and then the first Windows node following the docs here: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubeadm/upgrading-windows-nodes/

Every step ran without issue, but the kubelet service was not started. This was not immediately obvious, since "restart-service kubelet" does not propagate the error. I think "start-service kubelet" would be better advice.

The logs said: 

```
F0106 11:58:32.006122   17508 server.go:269] failed to run Kubelet: misconfiguration: kubelet cgroup driver: "systemd" is different from docker cgroup driver: "cgroupfs"
```

After changing the value of cgroupDriver manually in ```c:\var\lib\kubelet\config.yaml``` from "systemd" to "cgroupfs", the kubelet started successfully.

**What you expected to happen**:

One of 2 things: Either the Windows upgrade docs telling me what I need to do to fix this, or the kubeadm not breaking the configuration for windows in the first place.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. Add a windows node to a Kubernetes v1.19 cluster via kubeadm
2. Upgrade the cluster via kubeadm
3. Upgrade the Windows node following the docs [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubeadm/upgrading-windows-nodes/)

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.20.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Windows Server 2019 Core
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools: kubeadm
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

/sig windows
comments:
this may cause by the default value of defaultCgroupDriver  cgroupfs

Would you provide the `docker info` from Windows node?

> One of 2 things: Either the Windows upgrade docs telling me what I need to do to fix this, or the kubeadm not breaking the configuration for windows in the first place.

kubeadm doesn't do anything about cgroup drivers on Windows because cgroups don't exist on Windows.
ideally the kubelet checks about this should be skipped entirely in dockershim for non-Linux.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2010320/103771871-84819000-5063-11eb-9d35-9d7b377483f5.png)
However, windows docker return `cgroup driver` as cgroupfs.

probably `docker info`'s output is the same structure on all OSes with `cgroupfs` being a default value.
this field should not be checked on Windows at all.
/retitle kubelet: don't check for the Docker cgroup driver on Windows

adding `accepted` since the PR is favorable.
/triage accepted

review_comments:
minor change request here ~ can we log that we are skipping cgroup checks because it's windows ?

That will help make the kubelet logs for windows nodes easier to follow .
And also remind us to maybe do some equivalent steps at some point down the road , for windows
What would the equivalent steps be for Windows wrt cGroups? Maybe we should open an issue to track that?

i don't think there is a need for a note in the code or a separate tracking issue.

there is no "cgroup driver" concept on Windows as there is no "control group management" fragmentation due to multiple solutions.

it has Job objects:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/virtualization/windowscontainers/manage-containers/resource-controls
Thanks @neolit123. I agree there is no need for a note or an issue. Just wanted to ensure I was not missing something.
Ok... the comment is good enough I guess :)

Good idea. 

However, I have encounter kernel memory leak issues with 'cgroupfs' in some runc versions.
I'm not sure if we need to check the kernel version before overriding it.

to be consistent, it might be better to just always override and for a particular affected release in the supported version skew we can add this to "known issues" so that users can change distro / upgrade runc.

you can log an issue for the leaks, btw.
